Chapter.Section:
Counting prime numbers and finding the nth prime
The following functions require the program primecount by Kim Walisch to be installed on the system:
the number of prime numbers less than or equal to n.
As the combinatorial counting algorithm used by primecount is notably faster than O(n), it is feasible to count the primes less than, say, 10^{18} in about a minute. The maximum allowed argument is 10^{31} -- but for bounds of that order of magnitude, on a usual PC the computation would take too much resources anyway.
gap> PrimeCount(10^15); 29844570422669 gap> List([1..15],k->PrimeCount(Factorial(k))); [ 0, 1, 3, 9, 30, 128, 675, 4231, 30969, 258689, 2428956, 25306287, 289620751, 3610490805, 48686912930 ]
the n-th prime number.
gap> NthPrime(10^12); 29996224275833

ManSection.Returns: an iterator which iterates over the prime powers in increasing order, starting at 2 -- and ending at finish if specified.
